AcceptedOut.description: The answer to a request that is carried out later, by the worker.
AcceptedOut.title: AcceptedOut

CredentialCreate.description: A new provider credential. `base_url` is only for `openai_compatible`, which needs it.
CredentialCreate.title: CredentialCreate

ExportFilters.description: The trace-list filters. `from` and `to` are required and at most 90 days apart.
ExportFilters.title: ExportFilters

FallbackCondition.description: A failure after which the gateway moves on to the route's next target.
FallbackCondition.title: FallbackCondition

FallbackPolicy.description: The failures after which the gateway tries the next target. Empty means never.
FallbackPolicy.title: FallbackPolicy

FaultProfileCreate.description: A new fault profile. Omitted `params` are the scenario's defaults.
FaultProfileCreate.title: FaultProfileCreate

FaultProfileUpdate.description:
A partial edit: only the fields sent change.

`params` must be sent with `scenario` (they are only meaningful together); a `scenario`
sent without `params` resets the params to that scenario's defaults. `expires_at` is cleared
by sending `null`; every other field must have a value when it is sent. `changes()` tells an
absent field from one sent as `null`.
FaultProfileUpdate.title: FaultProfileUpdate

FaultScenario.description: A failure the gateway can inject (the Integration Lab); each has its own params.
FaultScenario.title: FaultScenario

GatewayKeyCreate.description:
A new gateway key. Without `route_id` it uses the project's default route.

A `None` limit means no limit; a `None` `cache_ttl_seconds` leaves the cache off.
GatewayKeyCreate.title: GatewayKeyCreate

GatewayKeyUpdate.description:
A partial edit: only the fields sent change.

The four nullable settings (`rpm_limit`, `tpm_limit`, `cache_ttl_seconds`, `fault_profile_id`)
are cleared by sending `null`; every other field must have a value when it is sent.
`changes()` tells an absent field from one sent as `null`.
GatewayKeyUpdate.title: GatewayKeyUpdate

GatewayOverviewOut.description:
Gateway traffic of a window of at most 7 days.

`errors` includes calls failed on purpose by Lab faults; `faults` says how many of the
requests carried one. `fallbacks` and `retries` are event counts, not request counts: the
switches to another target, and the repeated tries on one target, summed over all requests.
A latency is `null` when no request measured it.
GatewayOverviewOut.title: GatewayOverviewOut

InvitePreviewOut.description: What an invite grants, shown to the signed-in invitee before they accept.
InvitePreviewOut.title: InvitePreviewOut

LoginSignedInOut.description: The password (or the second step) was enough: the session cookies are set.
LoginSignedInOut.title: LoginSignedInOut

LoginTotpRequiredOut.description:
The password was right but the account has two-factor authentication: no cookies yet.

Send `challenge` with a code to `POST /auth/totp/verify` before `expires_at`.
LoginTotpRequiredOut.title: LoginTotpRequiredOut

MalformedJsonParams.description: A 200 whose body is cut to `keep_fraction` of its length; non-streaming calls only.
MalformedJsonParams.title: MalformedJsonParams

OAuthIdentityOut.description: A sign-in provider account linked to the caller.
OAuthIdentityOut.title: OAuthIdentityOut

OrgUpdateIn.description:
A change to the organization: any of its fields, and at least one.

A field that is left out is left alone; `null` is not a way to say that, so it is refused.
Strict about unknown fields, so a client that sends one this route does not handle is told
instead of being answered 200 with nothing changed.
OrgUpdateIn.title: OrgUpdateIn

RetryPolicy.description:
How often a target is tried, the first try included, and how long to wait in between.

The wait before retry *n* is `min(backoff_ms * 2 ** (n - 1), max_backoff_ms)`, replaced by a
provider's `Retry-After` when `honour_retry_after` is set.
RetryPolicy.title: RetryPolicy

RouteConfig.description:
Which credentials serve the route's calls, in fallback order, and how failures are handled.

`timeout_ms` is the whole budget for every attempt, wait and fallback of one call; for a
stream it bounds the time to the first byte.
RouteConfig.title: RouteConfig

RouteUpdateIn.description: A new config, and the version the client last read, which must still be the current one.
RouteUpdateIn.title: RouteUpdateIn

SlowResponseParams.description: The first byte of the response delayed by `delay_ms`.
SlowResponseParams.title: SlowResponseParams

Target.description: One provider credential the route can send a call to.
Target.title: Target

TimeoutParams.description: The call held for `hold_ms`, or what is left of the route's budget, then timed out.
TimeoutParams.title: TimeoutParams

TotpEnabledOut.description: The recovery codes, in clear text this once: the server keeps only their hashes.
TotpEnabledOut.title: TotpEnabledOut

TotpSetupOut.description: What to add to an authenticator app. Returned once; the secret is never shown again.
TotpSetupOut.title: TotpSetupOut

TruncatedStreamParams.description: A stream closed after `after_chunks` frames, without its end marker.
TruncatedStreamParams.title: TruncatedStreamParams

UnsupportedParameterParams.description: 400 naming `param` as unsupported by the model.
UnsupportedParameterParams.title: UnsupportedParameterParams

post.description:
Verify an address with the token from the emailed link.

No session is needed: the link is often opened in a browser that is not signed in, and the
token alone proves the inbox. Unknown, used, expired and wrong-kind tokens all answer the
same 404.
Send the signed-in user a fresh verification link, at most 3 per hour.

Check the password. A user with two-factor authentication gets a challenge, not a session.

The challenge is issued only after everything a session needs has held (throttle, password,
a password that is still current), so it means exactly "the first step passed".

schema.title: Response Login Api V1 Auth Login Post

get.description:
The caller's account and memberships: for a browser session, and for a personal access token.

This is the one `/auth` route a token may call, so a tool can check that its token works and
whose it is.

schema.title: Response List Identities Api V1 Auth Oauth Identities Get

get.description: The providers that can be used to sign in, so the login page shows only working buttons.

schema.title: Response List Providers Api V1 Auth Oauth Providers Get

delete.description: Unlink a provider account. The provider need not still be configured.

get.description:
Finish a sign-in or link, then redirect: to `next` on success, to an error page if not.

Every query parameter is optional so a callback that is wrong in any way still gets the
redirect the user can read, not a JSON validation error.

302.description: Redirect to `next` (with session cookies for a sign-in), or to `/login?error=<CODE>` (to `next` with `error=<CODE>` for a link). Clears `spl_oauth`.

get.description: Send the browser to the provider. `intent=link` links it to the signed-in user instead.

302.description: Redirect to the provider's sign-in page; sets `spl_oauth`.

post.description:
Email a reset link if the address has an account. The answer never says whether it does.

A known and an unknown address take the same path and get the same response: both are
counted by the limits first, and neither is turned away early. The only difference is that
a known address also gets a token and a queued email. The demo account counts as unknown.

Set a new password with the token from the emailed link.

No session is needed (the person forgot their password) and none is created: they sign in
afterwards with the new password. Every session of the account is ended. Unknown, used,
expired and wrong-kind tokens all answer the same 404.

delete.description: Sign out everywhere else: end every session of the user except the one making the call.

schema.title: Response List Sessions Api V1 Auth Sessions Get

get.description: The caller's tokens that can still be used. Never includes a secret.

schema.title: Response List Tokens Api V1 Auth Tokens Get

post.description: Create a token. The 201 is the only time its secret is shown.

delete.description: Revoke a token. Repeating it is fine; a token that is not the caller's is a 404.

post.description: Turn it off. Needs a valid code (TOTP or recovery), which is spent.
Turn it on with a code from the app. Returns the recovery codes, this once.
Make a secret for an authenticator app. Replaces one from an earlier, unconfirmed setup.

The second step of signing in: a challenge and a code make a session.

The user row is locked before the failure count is read, so concurrent attempts for one
account run one after another: the limit is exact, and a code cannot be spent twice. Wrong
codes are recorded as failed sign-ins, so they share the password's limit. A challenge issued
before the password changed is refused: it passed the first step against a password that no
longer exists.

get.description:
Show the org and role an invite grants, without accepting it.

Requires a signed-in user (the invitee), like accepting does. Unknown, used and expired
tokens all get the same 404, so the endpoint does not reveal which invites exist.

delete.description:
Delete the organization with its projects, traces, keys, members, invites and audit log.

Only an owner may, and only by typing the organization's slug as `confirm`. Everything goes
in one transaction: it is all deleted or none of it is. This is synchronous, which is fine for
the size of organization this runs; a very large one needs a background job.

patch.description:
Rename the organization, or require (or stop requiring) two-factor authentication.

`name` needs `org:update` (admins and owners) and `require_2fa` needs `org:security` (owners);
a request with both needs both, and is refused whole. Only values that change are applied and
audited, in one `org.update` event, so repeating a request is a no-op.

get.description:
The audit log, filtered like `GET /orgs/{org_id}/audit`, streamed as CSV (newest first).

A log with more than 50 000 matching events is refused before anything is sent.
get.summary: Download the audit log as CSV

get.description: Newest first. Never includes a key.

schema.title: Response List Credentials Api V1 Orgs  Org Id  Credentials Get

post.description:
Seal and store the key. `base_url` is required for `openai_compatible`, refused otherwise.

`409 NOT_CONFIGURED` without CREDENTIALS_KEYS; `422` on `base_url` for a URL that is not
`https://`, has userinfo, a query or a fragment, or resolves to a private address.

delete.description: `409 CREDENTIAL_IN_USE` while a gateway route sends calls through it.

post.description:
List the provider's models with the key and record the outcome as the last check.

A failing key is a `200` with `status: "error"` and a short reason such as `401 Unauthorized`.
Seal a new key in place of the old one. Clears the last check, which was of the old key.

schema.title: Response List Invites Api V1 Orgs  Org Id  Invites Get

post.description:
Create an invite and return its link; with an `email` and a sender, also mail it.

The invite, its audit event and the queued email commit in one transaction. Mailing only
changes how the link reaches someone: the invite is still accepted by any signed-in holder
of the link, whatever address it was mailed to.

schema.title: Response List Members Api V1 Orgs  Org Id  Members Get

get.description: Ordered by provider, pattern and start time.

schema.title: Response List Price Overrides Api V1 Orgs  Org Id  Price Overrides Get

post.description:
Rates are USD per million tokens. `effective_from` defaults to now.

The pattern matches a model exactly or with a snapshot suffix, like the seed prices.
`409 PRICE_OVERRIDE_EXISTS` when the organization already has one for the same provider,
pattern and start time.

delete.description: Spans ingested from now on fall back to the next price; stored costs are not rewritten.

schema.title: Response List Projects Api V1 Orgs  Org Id  Projects Get

get.description: The price table the server computes costs from. Any signed-in user, session or token.

schema.title: Response Get Prices Api V1 Prices Get

delete.description:
Delete the project with its traces, spans and API keys.

Admins and owners may, by typing the project's slug as `confirm`. The org's audit log keeps a
`project.delete` event with the name and slug, written in the same transaction.

get.description: Newest first. A finished export's `download_url` is a signed link, so nothing caches this.

post.description:
Queue an export of the traces matching `filters`; `from` and `to` are required.

Answers `409 NOT_CONFIGURED` when object storage is not set up. Poll `GET .../exports/{id}`
until `status` is `done`, then download from `download_url`.

The export's progress. `download_url` is a link valid for one hour, present once `done`.

Anyone holding that link can download the file until it expires, so nothing caches this.

post.description:
Delete every cached response of the project, whatever key stored it.

Idempotent: purging an empty cache succeeds. The audit event records how many entries went.

get.description: By name. `active` says whether a profile can fire now: enabled and not expired.

schema.title: Response List Profiles Api V1 Projects  Project Id  Gateway Fault Profiles Get

Omitted `params` are the scenario's defaults; a param that does not belong to the scenario
is `422` on `params.<name>`. `409 FAULT_PROFILE_NAME_TAKEN` for a name already used in the
project, and `422` on `expires_at` for a time that is not in the future.

delete.description: Delete the profile. Keys that ran it are detached and run no fault.

patch.description:
Change the fields sent; send `null` for `expires_at` to remove the expiry.

`params` must be sent with `scenario`; a `scenario` sent alone resets the params to that
scenario's defaults.

get.description: Newest first, revoked keys included. Unpaginated: a project keeps a handful of keys.

schema.title: Response List Keys Api V1 Projects  Project Id  Gateway Keys Get

post.description:
Create the key and return it with its `secret`, which is never shown again.

Without `route_id` the key uses the project's default route: `422 NO_DEFAULT_ROUTE` when the
project has none, and `422` on `route_id` for a route that is not the project's.

delete.description: Revoke the key. Apps using it get `401` from the next call. Revoking twice is a no-op.

patch.description:
Change the fields sent; send `null` to clear a limit or the cache TTL.

`404` for a revoked key: it can no longer be edited.

get.description:
Requests, errors, cache, fallbacks, latency and usage per target and key.

Counts every call that came through a gateway key, Lab faults included (`faults` says how
many). At most 7 days; longer is `422`.

post.description: Gateway keys created without a route use the default one. Not a new version.

Save the config of `version` again as a new version; the history is never rewritten.

`404` for a version the route never had; `422` when that config names a credential deleted
since.

get.description: Every saved config, newest first. `404` for an unknown route.
